question: What term describes the practice of assigning unpleasant ward chores to junior staff simply to avoid doing them yourself?

options.A: Effective mentorship
options.B: Right task assignment
options.C: Clinical supervision
options.D: Improper delegation

explanation: Dumping tasks inappropriately without regard for patient safety or fair workloads is considered improper delegation. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h7)

question: Why do older adults generally need fewer total calories each day compared to when they were younger?

options.A: They experience a drop in metabolism and muscle loss
options.B: They require much more sleep which burns stored body fat rapidly
options.C: Their stomach expands to hold larger portions of heavy foods
options.D: Their bodies completely stop absorbing carbohydrates and fats

explanation: As lean muscle mass declines and metabolic rate slows, the body burns fewer calories overall, meaning daily food intake must adjust. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T7#BMP118_U3_T7_h1)

question: Which group of babies is most at risk for Respiratory Distress Syndrome?

options.A: Preterm infants
options.B: Large-for-dates babies
options.C: Post-term infants
options.D: Infants born via elective caesarean section at term

explanation: Premature babies are born before their lungs can make enough surfactant, which leaves their air sacs prone to collapsing. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T5#BMP220_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why must midwives be extremely cautious when increasing milk feeds for a very low birth weight infant?

options.A: To prevent the development of necrotizing enterocolitis in an immature gut
options.B: To keep the infant's body temperature from dropping too rapidly
options.C: To stop the infant from developing severe neonatal jaundice immediately
options.D: To ensure the baby's kidneys do not filter out too much protein

explanation: Feeding an immature bowel too fast or with harsh formulas can cause tissue injury, inflammation, and death of the intestinal wall. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T1#BMP220_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which medication is routinely given during Nigerian antenatal clinics to prevent malaria?

options.A: Routine deworming tablets for all household pets
options.B: Antifungal creams for systemic fungal infections
options.C: Antibiotic prophylaxis for common skin rashes
options.D: Intermittent preventive treatment for malaria

explanation: Malaria is a major hazard in pregnancy, so sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine is given as intermittent preventive treatment during ANC visits. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T9#BMP212_U1_T9_h2)

question: A pregnant woman complains of sluggishness and asks which local food will give her sustained energy without sudden sugar crashes. What is the best recommendation?

options.A: White bread with sugary jam
options.B: Sponge cake made with refined white flour
options.C: Boiled sweet potatoes or yam with vegetables
options.D: Sweetened bottled fruit juice

explanation: Whole tubers and vegetables provide complex carbohydrates and fiber that release energy slowly into the bloodstream. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T1#BMP118_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common contributing factor to mastitis in nursing mothers?

options.A: Prolonged intervals between feeding times
options.B: Wearing tight clothing across the chest
options.C: Poor attachment of the baby to the breast
options.D: Frequent and demand-based breastfeeding

explanation: Feeding frequently helps drain the breasts effectively, which actually prevents milk stasis and mastitis rather than causing it. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T6#BMP214_U3_T6_h2)

question: Which procedure must NEVER be done when managing a patient with suspected placenta praevia?

options.A: Checking the fetal heart rate
options.B: Digital vaginal examination
options.C: Routine maternal blood grouping
options.D: Transabdominal ultrasound scan

explanation: Putting a finger into the vagina can touch the low-lying placenta and trigger heavy, dangerous bleeding. [learn more](BMP221_U2_T2#BMP221_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why is having a power backup like an inverter crucial for clinical teleconferencing?

options.A: It automatically lowers the cost of monthly data subscriptions
options.B: It eliminates background noise from the clinic environment
options.C: It improves the visual resolution of the computer monitor
options.D: It prevents sudden loss of connection during active patient discussions

explanation: Power cuts can abruptly terminate a session, disrupting critical clinical communications. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T4#BMP123_U4_T4_h4)

question: When is it permissible for a midwife to share confidential patient information?

options.A: When the midwife wants to discuss cases with friends outside work
options.B: Whenever a neighbor asks about the health status of a mother
options.C: When there is reasonable suspicion of child abuse or severe harm
options.D: As soon as a patient misses two consecutive antenatal appointments

explanation: The duty to protect a vulnerable child from abuse overrides the standard rules of medical confidentiality. [learn more](BMP222_U4_T4#BMP222_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why is the participation of practicing midwives important in applied research translation?

options.A: They prevent new medical technologies from entering hospitals
options.B: They are the only professionals legally allowed to write government laws
options.C: They conduct all laboratory experiments in university settings
options.D: They help bridge the gap between scientific findings and bedside care

explanation: Midwives work directly with mothers and are best positioned to implement new evidence-based practices in the maternity ward. [learn more](BMP225_U1_T6#BMP225_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary function of the gallbladder?

options.A: Filtering metabolic toxins
options.B: Secreting insulin into blood
options.C: Producing digestive enzymes
options.D: Storing and concentrating bile

explanation: The gallbladder holds bile produced by the liver and removes water to concentrate it until it is needed for digesting fats. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T1#BMP121_U2_T1_h5)

question: When should a midwife decide to modify a patient care plan?

options.A: Whenever a new nurse takes over the morning shift
options.B: When evaluation shows goals are consistently unmet
options.C: Only when the patient demands to leave the hospital
options.D: At the exact end of every single week of admission

explanation: Care plans are flexible tools that must be revised when evaluation proves current interventions are not producing the desired results. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T6#BMP120_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT part of secondary prevention for cervical cancer?

options.A: Conducting routine community awareness talks
options.B: Administering chemotherapy to a patient with Stage IV disease
options.C: Screening women with a Pap smear
options.D: Performing Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid (VIA)

explanation: Giving chemotherapy to treat advanced disease is a form of treatment, whereas screening and early detection tests represent secondary prevention. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T2#BMP320_U2_T2_h6)

question: When is a patient most likely to notice that their hernia bulge gets bigger?

options.A: While lying flat on their back
options.B: Right after drinking a glass of water
options.C: Immediately after sleeping through the night
options.D: When standing up or coughing

explanation: Gravity and increased pressure from standing or coughing push the hernia contents further out through the weak spot. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T8#BMP125_U3_T8_h4)

question: Which property lets a muscle fiber shorten forcefully when it receives a signal?

options.A: Elasticity
options.B: Extensibility
options.C: Contractility
options.D: Excitability

explanation: Contractility is the specific ability of muscle tissue to actively shorten and create a pulling force. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T8#BMP111_U1_T8_h5)

question: A patient has a severe fracture with bone pieces locked out of place and soft tissue caught in the break. Which reduction method will the surgical team likely choose?

options.A: Applying dry ice to shrink the swelling
options.B: Closed reduction with a simple bandage
options.C: Open reduction with internal fixation
options.D: Bed rest without any manipulation

explanation: When soft tissue gets trapped or closed manipulation fails, surgery is required to open the site and fix the bones with plates and screws. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T2#BMP216_U3_T2_h3)

question: Name the thick middle layer of the uterine wall made of smooth muscle.

options.A: Myometrium
options.B: Endometrium
options.C: Epimetrium
options.D: Perimetrium

explanation: The myometrium forms the muscular bulk of the uterus and drives contractions during childbirth. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T2#BMP210_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is the main role assigned to Traditional Birth Attendants in modern collaborative public health models?

options.A: Manufacturing synthetic oxytocin and intravenous fluids locally
options.B: Serving as official judges in medical malpractice lawsuits
options.C: Acting as community scouts to encourage early clinic referrals
options.D: Performing major obstetric surgeries in rural health posts

explanation: Collaborative programs leverage the trust and reach of TBAs to identify pregnant women and bring them into formal health facilities for safe deliveries. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T1#BMP215_U3_T1_h7)

question: When checking a pregnant woman's back alignment, which bony landmark is felt directly under the skin?

options.A: The vertebral foramen
options.B: The intervertebral disc
options.C: The transverse process
options.D: The spinous process

explanation: The spinous processes project straight back toward the skin surface, making them easy to feel along the midline of the back. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T8#BMP111_U2_T8_h2)

question: When does the final routine postnatal consultation usually take place?

options.A: At twenty-four hours postpartum
options.B: At six weeks postpartum
options.C: At six months postpartum
options.D: At two weeks postpartum

explanation: The six-week mark is the standard time for a final postnatal check to ensure full recovery and discuss family planning. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T3#BMP212_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which of these is an important warning sign that a patient with metrorrhagia should report immediately?

options.A: Needing to buy a calendar to track her periods
options.B: Mild fatigue after a normal day at work
options.C: Soaking through multiple heavy pads per hour
options.D: A slight change in her usual dietary preferences

explanation: Excessive bleeding that soaks through more than two pads an hour can signal a heavy hemorrhage that needs urgent medical attention. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T4#BMP310_U3_T4_h5)

question: A new mother develops a high fever, lower abdominal tenderness, and foul-smelling lochia three days after a manual placental removal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.A: Normal postpartum lochia transition
options.B: Secondary postpartum hemorrhage from atony
options.C: Acute urinary retention
options.D: Puerperal sepsis / endometritis

explanation: Fever, lower abdominal pain, and foul-smelling discharge after intrauterine procedures point strongly toward a uterine infection. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T3#BMP311_U4_T3_h8)

question: Which bone feature is commonly found in an anthropoid pelvis?

options.A: Prominent ischial spines
options.B: A side-to-side inlet wider than the front-to-back
options.C: A very wide subpubic arch
options.D: A short sacrum with four segments

explanation: The anthropoid pelvis typically features prominent ischial spines that can narrow the middle part of the pelvic cavity. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T5#BMP210_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the main goal of a vasectomy?

options.A: Preventing sexually transmitted infections
options.B: Permanent contraception
options.C: Boosting testosterone production
options.D: Treating prostate enlargement

explanation: A vasectomy is a permanent surgical method used to prevent pregnancy. It does not treat diseases or stop infections. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T13#BMP224_U3_T13_h1)

question: What is the primary way helminths survive inside a human host?

options.A: Feeding directly on solid bone tissues
options.B: Invading human red blood cells to reproduce
options.C: Absorbing nutrients directly from the host
options.D: Releasing toxic gases into the digestive tract

explanation: Helminths are parasitic worms that live inside the host and take nutrients away from the human body. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T8#BMP116_U3_T8_h1)

question: What is the main job of the upper limb compared to the lower limb?

options.A: Mobility and dexterity
options.B: Pelvic floor support
options.C: Spinal shock absorption
options.D: Weight-bearing stability

explanation: Upper limbs are built for moving around and doing fine motor tasks rather than carrying the full weight of the body. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T10#BMP111_U3_T10_h1)

question: What financial barrier frequently prevents young girls from accessing safe medical care?

options.A: Lack of personal income to pay for services
options.B: Expensive transport fares to foreign countries
options.C: High cost of government health insurance cards
options.D: Mandatory taxes placed on reproductive clinics

explanation: Because most adolescents are financially dependent, they cannot afford the fees charged by safe, regulated medical facilities. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h2)

question: How does untreated chlamydia threaten an ongoing pregnancy?

options.A: By stopping the production of normal amniotic fluid entirely
options.B: By blocking the absorption of dietary iron in the placenta
options.C: By increasing the risk of preterm labor and membrane rupture
options.D: By causing permanent high blood pressure in the mother's brain

explanation: Lower genital tract inflammation weakens fetal membranes and stimulates uterine contractions, leading to premature delivery. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T5#BMP310_U2_T5_h6)

question: What does an APGAR score of 2 at one minute tell the midwife?

options.A: The baby has mild distress and only requires warm blankets
options.B: The infant is severely depressed and needs immediate resuscitation
options.C: The newborn is transitioning normally and needs routine skin-to-skin
options.D: The delivery was completely free of any complications

explanation: A score of 0 to 3 falls in the severe depression range, necessitating immediate life-saving resuscitation. [learn more](BMP214_U1_T1#BMP214_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the main danger of dietary taboos that restrict meat and eggs during pregnancy?

options.A: They contribute to maternal nutritional deficiencies and anemia
options.B: They lower the mother's blood sugar to fatal levels instantly
options.C: They immediately trigger premature rupture of the membranes
options.D: They cause the unborn baby to grow dangerously large in size

explanation: Restricting protein foods deprives the mother of essential nutrients needed for blood production and fetal growth. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T3#BMP215_U3_T3_h2)

question: How does the ergometrine part of the drug help stop bleeding after birth?

options.A: By relaxing the cervical os to allow rapid passage of lochia
options.B: By lowering the general body temperature to slow down circulation
options.C: By dissolving any blood clots forming inside the uterine cavity
options.D: By causing a sustained tonic contraction that squeezes open blood vessels

explanation: Ergometrine makes the uterine muscle clamp down steadily. This action physically pinches off the open blood vessels where the placenta detached. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary underlying mechanism that causes breast engorgement?

options.A: Milk production outpacing milk removal
options.B: Too much water intake by the mother
options.C: A sudden drop in maternal estrogen levels
options.D: Blockage of the main milk ducts by fat

explanation: Engorgement happens when milk accumulates in the breast faster than the baby or a pump can remove it. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T4#BMP214_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is a main focus during the postnatal home visit around days three to five?

options.A: Administering the school-age booster vaccinations
options.B: Screening for neonatal jaundice and milk transition
options.C: Fitting the mother for permanent surgical sterilization
options.D: Assessing the baby for first tooth eruption

explanation: Days three to five mark when breast milk comes in fully and neonatal jaundice becomes most visible. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T4#BMP215_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which medication is commonly used for newborn eye prophylaxis in Nigerian maternity units?

options.A: Hydrocortisone ophthalmic suspension
options.B: Atropine sulfate eye drops
options.C: Dexamethasone eye ointment
options.D: Tetracycline 1% eye ointment

explanation: Tetracycline 1% ointment is standard, stable, and affordable for use across Nigerian health facilities. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T2#BMP220_U2_T2_h4)

question: Where do T lymphocytes go to finish their maturation?

options.A: Bone marrow
options.B: Thymus gland
options.C: Lymph node
options.D: Spleen

explanation: T cells originate in the bone marrow but travel to the thymus gland to mature and gain immune function. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T3#BMP111_U5_T3_h4)

question: Which condition is most commonly linked to placental abruption?

options.A: Gestational gestational diabetes
options.B: Iron deficiency anaemia
options.C: Asymptomatic bacteriuria
options.D: Pregnancy-induced hypertension

explanation: High blood pressure damages the blood vessels that supply the placenta, making the tissue more likely to detach early. [learn more](BMP221_U2_T1#BMP221_U2_T1_h4)

question: A mother asks if she should apply herbal powder to her baby's wet cord stump. How should the midwife respond?

options.A: Suggest mixing the powder with palm oil for better results
options.B: Agree only if the baby develops a mild fever first
options.C: Advise against it because herbs and powders can introduce germs and cause infection
options.D: Encourage it if the powder was prepared by an older family member

explanation: Unsterile home substances like herbs and powders easily carry tetanus spores and other bacteria directly into the open umbilical wound. [learn more](BMP214_U2_T3#BMP214_U2_T3_h2)

question: What primary substance is lacking in the lungs of a preterm infant, leading to Respiratory Distress Syndrome?

options.A: Bilirubin
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Hemoglobin
options.D: Surfactant

explanation: Surfactant reduces surface tension inside the tiny air sacs, and its absence causes the lungs to collapse easily with every breath. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T1#BMP220_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which of these is an example of an action word that can be easily measured in a clinical learning objective?

options.A: Understand
options.B: Demonstrate
options.C: Know
options.D: Appreciate

explanation: Demonstrate is an observable action that an examiner can watch and grade, unlike abstract words like understand or appreciate. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T3#BMP312_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which major class of antifungal drugs works by stopping the production of ergosterol in the fungal cell membrane?

options.A: Polyenes
options.B: Echinocandins
options.C: Nucleoside analogues
options.D: Azoles

explanation: Azole antifungals block key fungal enzymes, stopping the production of ergosterol and weakening the cell membrane. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T2#BMP116_U3_T2_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal responsibility when monitoring a patient's heart status in clinical practice?

options.A: Monitoring laboratory results for abnormal potassium and calcium levels
options.B: Surgically repairing damaged coronary arteries at the bedside
options.C: Screening for physical signs of chest discomfort or respiratory distress
options.D: Assessing vital signs and tracking trends in maternal blood pressure

explanation: Bedside surgery on coronary arteries is performed by specialized surgeons in an operating theatre, not as a general nursing task. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T3#BMP111_U3_T3_h7)

question: Which gland in the body produces growth hormone to stimulate bone elongation and tissue building?

options.A: Adrenal gland
options.B: Pituitary gland
options.C: Pancreas
options.D: Thyroid gland

explanation: The anterior pituitary gland secretes growth hormone, which drives physical growth. [learn more](BMP222_U1_T2#BMP222_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is time so critical during an obstetric emergency in a home birth setting?

options.A: The requirement to fill out paperwork before leaving
options.B: The absence of immediate surgical intervention at home
options.C: The need to wait for family permission to transfer
options.D: The delay caused by calling local community leaders

explanation: Because a home does not have operating theatres or blood banks, waiting too long to move a patient with a severe complication puts her life at extreme risk. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T5#BMP215_U2_T5_h1)

question: When should a midwife expect medical staff to start drug therapy for a client with gestational diabetes?

options.A: Only after the baby shows signs of severe intrauterine growth restriction
options.B: Immediately upon confirming a positive 75-gram OGTT result
options.C: As soon as the fasting blood sugar crosses 4.0 mmol/L at the booking visit
options.D: When diet and lifestyle changes fail to keep blood glucose within target ranges

explanation: Medication is added only when healthy meal planning and exercise are not enough to keep blood sugar levels in the safe target range. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T2#BMP221_U4_T2_h6)

question: What childhood condition increases a boy's chance of developing testicular cancer later in life?

options.A: Hypospadias
options.B: Phimosis
options.C: Cryptorchidism
options.D: Hydrocele

explanation: Cryptorchidism, or an undescended testicle, places the tissue in a warmer area of the body, which raises the risk of cancer over time. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T5#BMP320_U2_T5_h2)

question: How do community mobilization strategies improve antenatal care attendance in rural areas?

options.A: By eliminating all transportation costs
options.B: By forcing husbands to pay fines
options.C: By building trust through local leaders and addressing cultural fears
options.D: By replacing trained midwives

explanation: Working with community leaders helps clear up misunderstandings and encourages local women to trust and use the nearby health facility. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T2#BMP126_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following conditions is NOT a reason to avoid giving an implant?

options.A: Current breast cancer diagnosis
options.B: A history of mild uncomplicated malaria last year
options.C: Active severe liver disease
options.D: Unexplained vaginal bleeding awaiting diagnosis

explanation: Past mild infections like malaria do not affect hormonal implant safety, unlike serious conditions such as liver disease or breast cancer. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T7#BMP224_U3_T7_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of food hygiene measures across the food chain?

options.A: Enhancing the market value of farm produce
options.B: Eliminating the need for food preservation
options.C: Ensuring safety and wholesomeness of food
options.D: Accelerating the cooking time of meals

explanation: Food hygiene focuses specifically on keeping food safe and wholesome from production all the way to final consumption. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T5#BMP117_U4_T5_h1)

question: Which built-in utility helps you check for frozen programs and high processor usage?

options.A: Antivirus scanner
options.B: Disk defragmenter
options.C: Task Manager
options.D: Control Panel

explanation: Task Manager displays all currently running applications and shows how much memory and processing power each one uses. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T4#BMP123_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which sign shows that a child with pneumonia needs urgent oxygen therapy?

options.A: Low-grade evening fever
options.B: Central cyanosis
options.C: Occasional sneezing
options.D: Mild clear nasal discharge

explanation: Cyanosis, or a bluish discoloration of the tongue and lips, points to critically low blood oxygen levels requiring immediate supplementation. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T10#BMP222_U2_T10_h5)

question: What two main types of hormones are found in combined oral contraceptive pills?

options.A: FSH and LH
options.B: Estrogen and progestin
options.C: Testosterone and progesterone
options.D: Oxytocin and prolactin

explanation: COCs are named because they combine a synthetic estrogen and a progestin to mimic female reproductive hormones. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T4#BMP224_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the main focus of transformational leadership compared to strict, rules-based approaches?

options.A: Minimising financial expenses within the maternity unit
options.B: Shared vision, personal growth, and emotional connection
options.C: Strict adherence to hospital administrative protocols
options.D: Enforcing rigid shift discipline among junior nurses

explanation: Transformational leadership moves beyond simple rule-following to inspire staff through shared goals and mutual support. [learn more](BMP312_U1_T6#BMP312_U1_T6_h1)

question: You notice a soft swelling on a newborn's head that crosses the suture lines. What is the best first step?

options.A: Document the finding accurately and report it to the doctor.
options.B: Tell the mother that her baby suffered permanent brain damage.
options.C: Attempt to drain the fluid using a sterile syringe immediately.
options.D: Ignore the swelling because all head bumps disappear within hours.

explanation: Findings like a caput succedaneum should be documented clearly and reported for proper medical follow-up. [learn more](BMP214_U1_T2#BMP214_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is considered the gold standard psychological treatment for specific phobias?

options.A: Daily high-dose vitamin injections
options.B: Immediate surgical intervention
options.C: Long-term strict bed rest
options.D: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy

explanation: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy helps patients examine and change unhelpful thought patterns and behaviors linked to their phobic triggers. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T6#BMP223_U3_T6_h6)

question: Name ONE common food source that is rich in natural phytoestrogens.

options.A: Soybeans and related products
options.B: Pasteurised whole cow milk
options.C: Highly refined white sugar
options.D: Processed red meat products

explanation: Legumes, especially soybeans, contain plant compounds called phytoestrogens that weakly interact with oestrogen receptors in the body. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T5#BMP320_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which finding is typically discovered during an abdominal examination of a woman with obstructed labor?

options.A: A completely relaxed and soft uterus
options.B: Low maternal pulse and resting blood pressure
options.C: An easily ballotable fetal head above the pelvic brim
options.D: A visible and palpable Bandl's ring

explanation: The overworked upper segment and stretched lower segment create a distinct ridge crossing the abdomen during obstruction. [learn more](BMP311_U2_T3#BMP311_U2_T3_h3)

question: When would a midwife most likely suggest using a specialized soy-based formula for an infant?

options.A: The baby reaches the age of six months and starts solids
options.B: The baby has a diagnosed allergy to cow's milk protein
options.C: The mother wants the baby to grow faster than average
options.D: The family cannot afford the standard starter milk brand

explanation: Soy-based formulas provide an alternative protein source for infants who experience allergic reactions to cow's milk proteins. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T8#BMP214_U3_T8_h3)

question: In the PICO framework, what does the letter 'I' stand for?

options.A: Intervention
options.B: Investigation
options.C: Incidence
options.D: Indicator

explanation: The 'I' in PICO represents the specific treatment, care practice, or test being evaluated in the study. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T1#BMP225_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is the main reason for closing a perineal wound in separate anatomical layers?

options.A: To prevent dead space and reduce the risk of blood pooling
options.B: To allow the outer skin stitches to dissolve much faster
options.C: To make the scar completely invisible within a few weeks
options.D: To increase the overall tightness of the pelvic floor muscles

explanation: Layered closure eliminates empty spaces where blood can collect and form painful clots, supporting proper healing. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T6#BMP212_U3_T6_h5)

question: Why is measuring head circumference important during the first two years of life?

options.A: It predicts the final adult height of the child accurately.
options.B: It tracks the closure of the posterior fontanelle exclusively.
options.C: It monitors normal brain growth and detects cranial abnormalities.
options.D: It measures the overall nutritional status of skeletal muscles.

explanation: Head circumference directly reflects brain volume expansion during infancy, helping catch conditions like hydrocephalus early. [learn more](BMP222_U1_T1#BMP222_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is a common misconception about colostrum that midwives frequently encounter?

options.A: It is produced in excessive quantities
options.B: It causes immediate infant weight gain
options.C: It cures all childhood infections instantly
options.D: It is dirty and should be discarded

explanation: A widespread myth is that the yellowish first milk is stale or harmful, whereas it is actually lifesaving and protective. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h6)

question: What is the typical range of vaginal pH in a patient with a simple yeast infection?

options.A: Highly alkaline range above 7.5
options.B: Normal acidic range between 4.0 and 4.5
options.C: Neutral range sitting strictly at 7.0
options.D: Exceedingly acidic range below 2.0

explanation: Unlike other vaginal infections that raise the pH, yeast infections generally do not change the normal acidic balance of the vagina. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T8#BMP310_U2_T8_h4)

question: What does the term generalizability mean when reading a research paper?

options.A: Whether the introduction section is written clearly
options.B: How many generals or high-ranking officers funded the study
options.C: How fast the statistical software generated the p-value

question: Which of these is NOT strictly needed to run a safe daily maternity unit?

question: A midwife student wants to study why pregnant teenagers fail to attend antenatal clinics using a pre-existing psychological model of health behavior. What is this model called in the research proposal?

options.A: A statistical formula

question: When do pregnant and postnatal women learn most effectively during health education sessions?

question: How does showing genuine empathy primarily help a pregnant woman in the clinic?

question: Which action must you strictly avoid when managing a case of shoulder dystocia?

options.D: Applying fundal pressure

question: Why is hydralazine given in small, repeated doses rather than all at once?

options.B: To prevent the development of permanent drug tolerance

options.D: To prevent a sudden, dangerous drop in maternal blood pressure

question: An undernourished toddler presents with severe untreated diaper rash, chronic hunger, and missed immunizations even though the parents have enough money. What type of maltreatment is most likely happening?

options.A: Active physical abuse
options.B: Physical neglect
options.C: Psychological abuse

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard responsibility of the mental health nurse in the community?

options.A: Providing supportive counseling and health education
options.B: Performing complex major brain surgery for trauma victims
options.C: Monitoring medication compliance and managing side effects
options.D: Referring clients to specialized psychiatric care units

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature evaluated during a physical assessment of clubfoot?

question: What causes physiological anemia of pregnancy to appear on standard laboratory blood tests?

question: A woman in labor in a warm delivery room sweats heavily from her forehead and chest. Which glands cause this cooling response?

options.A: Ceruminous glands
options.B: Eccrine glands
options.C: Sebaceous glands
options.D: Apocrine glands

question: Why is establishing a baseline at the first booking visit important?

options.A: It completely prevents all future pregnancy complications

question: A nursing mother wakes up several times at night to feed her baby before taking her morning temperature. How will this affect her chart?

options.A: Her chart will automatically show when ovulation happens
options.B: Her temperature readings may become erratic and difficult to interpret
options.C: Her basal temperature will permanently drop to zero

question: When introducing new foods to an infant, what practice is recommended?

options.A: Stop breastfeeding entirely on the day foods begin
options.B: Mix multiple new foods together on the very first day
options.C: Add plenty of hot chili spices to stimulate appetite
options.D: Introduce one single food at a time to check for reactions

question: Which of these actions is NOT safe when transferring a woman with active antepartum haemorrhage to a higher-level facility?

question: Why is head flexion so important for the baby during labor?

question: A midwife wants to send a monthly maternity report to the hospital director while keeping her own master copy safe in her department folder. What should she do?

options.C: Rename the report file extension to a different format
options.D: Copy the report file and place the duplicate in the director's folder

explanation: Copying allows her to share a duplicate version of the document while keeping her original master file secure in its original location. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T3#BMP123_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the main reason why proper nutrition is so important during the postpartum period?

options.D: Accelerating infant dental eruption

question: Why do patients with advanced chronic kidney disease frequently develop severe anemia?

options.C: Patients refuse to eat green vegetables and red meat
options.D: Dialysis machines actively destroy all circulating platelets

question: What term describes passing an infection from a mother to her baby during pregnancy or childbirth?

question: A young mother requests an intrauterine device, but the midwife refuses, stating she is too young and has no children yet. Which principle has the midwife violated?

options.B: Mandatory hospital documentation guidelines

question: Which postnatal patient needs the closest observation for blood clot complications?

question: What happens to the glomerular filtration rate during a normal pregnancy?

question: A community health nurse finds several pupils scratching itchy patches on their scalps during a morning assembly. Which school health objective does addressing this directly support?

question: If a pregnant patient with DKA receives saline and her blood sugar drops to 200 mg/dL, what change in her IV fluids should be expected?

question: What is the main reason for ordering a full blood count for a patient with metrorrhagia?

question: What is the main role of a midwife working in a Nigerian Primary Health Care Centre?

question: What dangerous practice must midwives actively discourage when a child swallows kerosene or bleach?

question: Why is counseling before a vasectomy so important?

question: What is the recommended standard practice for routine umbilical cord care to prevent infection?

question: During a power outage in a primary health center in Nigeria, what is the best method to warm a low-birth-weight infant?

question: An infant receiving IV rehydration is now alert, demanding feeds, and has stopped vomiting. What is the best next step?

question: Why must a midwife wash instruments with soap and water AFTER soaking them in chlorine, rather than skipping the wash step?

question: How does vitamin D help the body manage phosphorus?

question: Which body area is most typical for accidental bruises on a normally active toddler?

question: Why is birth-spacing counseling especially important after a caesarean section?

question: A nurse checks a patient's stoma on the first day after surgery and finds it looks dark purple and dry. What should the nurse do first?

question: Why is the ABO system considered so critical in clinical practice?

question: Why must primary health care look beyond traditional medical settings to achieve true community well-being?

question: Why does the official definition of a midwife specifically emphasize partnership with women?

question: What is the most common category of chronic hypertension seen in pregnant women?

question: How does preventing calcium entry help to stop uterine contractions?

options.C: Hemoglobin
options.D: Myoglobin

explanation: Calcium binds to calmodulin in smooth muscle, taking the place of troponin which is used in skeletal muscle. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T2#BMP111_U3_T2_h4)

question: What primary substance builds up in the body to cause neonatal jaundice?

options.A: Free biliverdin
options.B: Maternal hemoglobin
options.C: Conjugated albumin
options.D: Unconjugated bilirubin

explanation: Jaundice appears when fat-soluble unconjugated bilirubin accumulates faster than the newborn liver can process and clear it. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T6#BMP220_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why do barrier methods generally have higher pregnancy rates in real-life use compared to implants?

options.A: They depend on the user remembering to use them every time
options.B: Body heat weakens the barrier material over months
options.C: They expire within twenty-four hours of manufacture
options.D: They dissolve completely inside the body fluids

explanation: Human error or forgetting to use a barrier during intercourse leads to higher accidental pregnancy rates. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T2#BMP126_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which combination of medicines is usually given first when treating suspected neonatal sepsis?

options.A: Ampicillin and Gentamicin
options.B: Erythromycin and Tetracycline
options.C: Metronidazole and Nystatin
options.D: Paracetamol and Ibuprofen

explanation: Ampicillin paired with an aminoglycoside like gentamicin provides broad coverage against the most common early-onset newborn infections. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T1#BMP220_U2_T1_h6)

question: A client wants to use the Standard Days Method. Her last three cycles were 24 days, 35 days, and 28 days. What is your best action?

options.A: Tell her to wait one more month and check her cycle length again.
options.B: Recommend she use barrier methods only during her period days.
options.C: Enroll her immediately because one of her cycles is in the correct range.
options.D: Advise her to choose a different family planning method due to cycle irregularity.

explanation: Having cycles outside the 26 to 32 day range means the method is not safe for her, as unpredictability raises the risk of pregnancy during the fertile window. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T1#BMP224_U4_T1_h2)

question: A client in a Nigerian antenatal clinic wants to use the TwoDay Method but expresses concern that vaginal discharge from a mild infection might confuse her tracking. What is the best action for the midwife?

options.A: Suggest she use hormonal contraceptives until the next menstrual cycle
options.B: Treat the infection first and teach her how to separate infection discharge from fertile mucus
options.C: Tell her to switch immediately to daily basal body temperature charting
options.D: Advise her to ignore all discharge and assume she is infertile

explanation: Infections can alter vaginal secretions, so treating underlying conditions and educating the client on recognizing normal patterns ensures accurate method use. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T2#BMP224_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why is head circumference measured routinely in a newborn with myelomeningocele?

options.A: To monitor for early signs of hydrocephalus
options.B: To assess the maturity of facial bones
options.C: To determine the required dose of vitamin K
options.D: To calculate the exact birth weight percentile

explanation: Many babies with open spinal defects also develop hydrocephalus, which causes fluid buildup and rapid head enlargement. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T3#BMP220_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is searching for grey literature especially important for maternal health research in Nigeria?

options.A: It is the only way to access expensive paid articles without a subscription
options.B: Government documents contain zero risk of methodological bias or errors
options.C: Many local health policies and hospital audits are never published in international journals
options.D: International databases automatically translate all Nigerian languages into English

explanation: Crucial local data often sits in government or institutional reports rather than global academic indexes. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T1#BMP225_U2_T1_h3)

question: A patient with glomerulonephritis gains two kilograms in a single day. What does this finding most likely indicate?

options.A: The patient has successfully healed from the infection
options.B: The patient is retaining excess fluid in the body
options.C: The patient has started eating too much high-protein food
options.D: The patient is building healthy new muscle tissue rapidly

explanation: Rapid weight gain in a short period is a classic sign of fluid retention and worsening edema. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T4#BMP216_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why are premature infants at a higher risk of low blood sugar right after birth?

options.A: They lose too much body heat through their thin skin layers
options.B: They digest breast milk much faster than term babies do
options.C: They have very limited glycogen stores and immature metabolic pathways
options.D: Their mothers always have high blood sugar during late pregnancy

explanation: Babies born early miss out on the final weeks of pregnancy when significant glycogen and fat stores are normally built up in the liver. [learn more](BMP220_U3_T2#BMP220_U3_T2_h1)

question: How should a newly applied plaster of Paris cast be handled while it is still damp?

options.A: Lifted using only fingertips
options.B: Placed directly under a heat fan
options.C: Supported gently with flat palms
options.D: Wrapped tightly in heavy plastic

explanation: Using fingertips creates deep indentations in soft plaster, which can press into the underlying skin and cause dangerous pressure ulcers. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T2#BMP216_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is the final step a midwife takes after completing the medical history, physical examination, and screening?

options.A: Synthesizing the findings to help the client choose a safe, suitable method
options.B: Mandating that the client return every week for repeat examinations
options.C: Filing the client records away without discussing the results
options.D: Directing the client to purchase whatever method is cheapest in the market

explanation: Bringing all assessment details together allows the midwife and client to make a collaborative, safe choice. [learn more](BMP224_U2_T2#BMP224_U2_T2_h8)

question: Why is an emergency hysterectomy considered a treatment of absolute last resort in severe postpartum haemorrhage?

options.A: It permanently removes the woman's ability to bear future children
options.B: It requires general anaesthesia which is unavailable in clinics
options.C: It automatically causes severe kidney failure
options.D: It takes longer to perform than any other surgery

explanation: While it saves the mother's life, removing the uterus destroys her future fertility, so surgeons try all conservative methods first. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T1#BMP311_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is the main objective of secondary prevention in healthcare?

options.A: Early diagnosis and prompt treatment of existing disease
options.B: Preventing a healthy person from ever contracting an infection
options.C: Promoting general community wealth and clean water access
options.D: Rehabilitating a patient with permanent physical disabilities

explanation: Secondary prevention catches conditions early through screening so they can be treated before causing severe harm. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T1#BMP117_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the role of viremia in chickenpox?

options.A: It keeps the virus inside the respiratory tract
options.B: It carries the virus through the bloodstream to the skin and organs
options.C: It triggers antibodies that destroy the virus instantly
options.D: It creates permanent immunity in the lymph nodes without a rash

explanation: Viremia means the virus is traveling through the blood, which allows it to reach the skin and cause the typical rash. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T4#BMP222_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which measurement represents the transverse diameter of the pelvic outlet?

options.A: Obstetric conjugate
options.B: Diagonal conjugate
options.C: Bisischial diameter
options.D: Interspinous diameter

explanation: The bisischial diameter measures the distance between the two ischial tuberosities at the pelvic outlet. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T2#BMP210_U1_T2_h4)

question: How does selective pressure work during an antibiotic course?

options.A: It stops human white blood cells from producing antibodies
options.B: It removes all bacteria from the body within five minutes
options.C: It forces resistant bacteria to turn into harmless human cells
options.D: It kills weak bacteria and lets resistant survivors multiply

explanation: The medication eliminates the sensitive bacteria strains, leaving any resistant mutants behind to multiply without competition. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T9#BMP116_U2_T9_h4)

question: What type of medication is prescribed to cure a viral mumps infection?

options.A: A strong course of broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: None, because antibiotics do not kill viruses
options.C: Antifungal syrups taken three times daily
options.D: Specific antiviral tablets given intravenously

explanation: Mumps is viral, so management relies entirely on supportive care while the child's immune system fights off the infection naturally. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T2#BMP222_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the most important sign that a newborn resuscitation is working?

options.A: Urine output
options.B: Heart rate
options.C: Body temperature
options.D: Skin color

explanation: Heart rate response tells the midwife immediately whether ventilation is successfully oxygenating the newborn. [learn more](BMP214_U2_T2#BMP214_U2_T2_h6)

question: A woman in active labor breathes very rapidly and deeply during strong contractions. What immediate blood gas change is she most likely experiencing?

options.A: A complete failure of her peripheral chemoreceptors
options.B: A drop in carbon dioxide leading to alkalosis
options.C: A dangerous drop in arterial oxygen saturation
options.D: A massive increase in carbon dioxide causing acidosis

explanation: Rapid, deep breathing blows off excessive amounts of carbon dioxide, which reduces acid levels and raises blood pH into an alkaline state. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T5#BMP121_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which of these is a common supply challenge in primary health clinics?

options.A: An excess of medical textbooks
options.B: Too many working ultrasound machines
options.C: Stock-outs of contraceptive supplies
options.D: Over-staffing of trained midwives

explanation: Frequent stock-outs of commodities disrupt service delivery and turn clients away when they are ready to adopt a method. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T3#BMP224_U1_T3_h4)

question: What daily dietary requirement classifies a mineral as a macro mineral?

options.A: Exceeding 10 grams daily
options.B: Less than 1 milligram daily
options.C: Exactly 50 milligrams daily
options.D: Exceeding 100 milligrams daily

explanation: Minerals needed in amounts greater than 100 milligrams per day are called macro minerals, separating them from trace elements. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T8#BMP118_U2_T8_h1)

question: How many individual vertebrae make up the thoracic region of the spine?

options.A: Thirty-three vertebrae
options.B: Seven vertebrae
options.C: Twelve vertebrae
options.D: Five vertebrae

explanation: The thoracic region contains twelve vertebrae that connect directly to the rib cage in the upper and mid back. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T8#BMP111_U2_T8_h1)

question: A woman visits the primary health clinic for a postnatal checkup. What should the midwife mainly check?

options.A: Visual acuity and blood cholesterol lipid profiles
options.B: Surgical site infection from a previous appendectomy
options.C: Range of motion in the lower lumbar spine joints
options.D: Uterine involution, lochia, and breastfeeding success

explanation: Postnatal checks focus on how the mother's body is recovering, checking lochia, and ensuring breastfeeding is going well. [learn more](BMP215_U1_T2#BMP215_U1_T2_h2)

question: A patient recovering from a tonsillectomy swallows frequently while resting in bed. What complication should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Normal healing of the surgical site
options.B: A sudden allergic reaction to water
options.C: Severe hunger from missed meals
options.D: Postoperative bleeding in the throat

explanation: Frequent swallowing while at rest is a classic early warning sign that blood is trickling down the back of the throat. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T2#BMP125_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is securing the Tenckhoff catheter to the skin important for infection control?

options.A: It stops the tube from pulling and creating small wounds that germs can enter.
options.B: It prevents the glucose in the dialysate from turning into crystals.
options.C: It warms up the dialysate fluid before it reaches internal organs.
options.D: It increases the speed at which waste products leave the bloodstream.

explanation: Anchoring the catheter prevents friction and movement at the exit site, reducing micro-trauma that serves as an entry point for bacteria. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T9#BMP216_U1_T9_h6)

question: Why are feeding bottles discouraged in favor of cups when giving liquids to infants?

options.A: Infants are physically incapable of sucking from a bottle teat
options.B: Bottles cause immediate vitamin deficiency in growing toddlers
options.C: Cups promote faster speech development than bottles
options.D: Bottles are difficult to clean thoroughly and easily harbor harmful bacteria

explanation: The narrow parts of feeding bottles trap milk residue and germs, which frequently leads to infant diarrhea. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T3#BMP118_U3_T3_h6)

question: Which simple tool is most commonly used in busy clinics to quickly screen acute malnutrition without needing a weighing scale?

options.A: A flexible wooden height rod
options.B: Mid-upper arm circumference tape
options.C: A mercury sphygmomanometer
options.D: Standard obstetric pelvimeter

explanation: MUAC tape is portable, quick, and highly effective for rapid nutritional screening in community settings. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T1#BMP118_U4_T1_h2)

question: How does adding glucose to the dialysate help remove extra water from the body?

options.A: It forces the kidneys to produce more urine through hormones.
options.B: It creates an osmotic pressure gradient that pulls water across the membrane.
options.C: It raises blood pressure to push fluid faster through the urinary tract.
options.D: It directly breaks water molecules down into harmless gas.

explanation: Glucose acts as an osmotic agent, making the dialysate hypertonic compared to blood, which naturally draws excess water across the peritoneal membrane via osmosis. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T9#BMP216_U1_T9_h2)

question: Which of the following organisms is classified as a protozoan?

options.A: Taenia solium
options.B: Ascaris lumbricoides
options.C: Sarcoptes scabiei
options.D: Plasmodium species

explanation: Plasmodium, the parasite that causes malaria, is a single-celled microscopic protozoan. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T3#BMP116_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the best approach when looking at a complex statistical output table for the first time?

options.A: Change the numbers in the table until they match your expectations
options.B: Guess the final conclusion without looking at the sample size
options.C: Delete every row that contains a decimal point to make it simpler
options.D: Focus on the specific columns and values that answer your research question

explanation: Outputs contain a lot of extra technical details, so targeting the specific metrics related to your objectives prevents confusion. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T5#BMP225_U4_T5_h6)

question: A couple comes to the clinic struggling to conceive after fourteen months. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Tell the woman to stop working outside the home
options.B: Refer them immediately for expensive IVF
options.C: Prescribe strong hormone pills to the woman
options.D: Take a detailed medical and reproductive history from both partners

explanation: Care always starts with a thorough history from both partners to help guide the next steps and tests. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T6#BMP224_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is the primary cause of portal hypertension in conditions like liver cirrhosis?

options.A: Weakening of the heart muscle reducing cardiac output
options.B: Blockage of the inferior vena cava near the diaphragm
options.C: Obstruction of blood flow through the liver due to scarring
options.D: Excessive fluid intake increasing overall blood volume

explanation: Scar tissue in a damaged liver creates resistance, causing blood to back up and raise pressure within the portal vein network. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T19#BMP111_U5_T19_h5)

question: A client trying to conceive asks why her basal body temperature rises slightly in the second half of her cycle. What physiological explanation should the midwife give?

options.A: The developing placenta releases adrenaline to increase maternal energy.
options.B: Metabolic activity inside the maturing oocyte generates excess body heat.
options.C: Estrogen surge right before ovulation causes a temporary fever.
options.D: Progesterone released by the corpus luteum raises core body temperature.

explanation: Progesterone has a thermogenic effect on the hypothalamus, causing a measurable rise in basal body temperature following ovulation. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T4#BMP210_U2_T4_h6)

question: What condition can a newborn baby get after passing through a birth canal affected by a maternal yeast infection?

options.A: Oral thrush
options.B: Neonatal tetanus
options.C: Congenital malaria
options.D: Jaundice

explanation: Babies can pick up Candida yeast during a vaginal birth, which often shows up as white patches inside their mouth called oral thrush. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h7)

question: What happens to the decidua capsularis as the fetus and amniotic sac grow during pregnancy?

options.A: It thickens into a muscular wall that takes over the function of the myometrium.
options.B: It stretches, thins out, and eventually fuses with the decidua parietalis.
options.C: It transforms directly into the umbilical cord to supply oxygen to the fetus.
options.D: It detaches from the uterus and is expelled through the cervix every trimester.

explanation: As the pregnancy sac expands, the decidua capsularis gets pushed outward until it merges with the opposite uterine wall. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T4#BMP210_U4_T4_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recognized pelvic shape in obstetrics?

options.A: Android
options.B: Gynecoid
options.C: Platypelloid
options.D: Pyramidal

explanation: The four classic pelvic shapes are gynecoid, android, anthropoid, and platypelloid; pyramidal is not one of them. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T1#BMP210_U1_T1_h6)

question: A pregnant woman at 10 weeks mentions she had a cone biopsy two years ago. What should the midwife do?

options.A: Reassure her that past cervical surgeries have no effect
options.B: Note it as a risk factor and arrange early ultrasound monitoring
options.C: Schedule an immediate emergency C-section
options.D: Advise her to stay on strict bed rest all pregnancy

explanation: A prior cone biopsy is a mechanical risk factor, so checking the cervical length early with an ultrasound helps keep a close, safe watch. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h3)

question: When is it ethically okay for a midwife to share a client's medical information?

options.A: When hospital management wants to increase community publicity
options.B: To share interesting clinical cases with friends outside work
options.C: When there is clear danger of severe harm to the client or a minor
options.D: Whenever a curious family member asks about the client's visit

explanation: Confidentiality can be overridden in rare emergencies involving severe harm or legal mandates to protect vulnerable individuals. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T5#BMP224_U1_T5_h6)

question: What does Premature Rupture of Membranes (PROM) mean at term?

options.A: Membranes stay intact until the second stage of active labor
options.B: Water breaks after regular painful contractions have started
options.C: Water breaks before labor contractions start at 37 weeks or later
options.D: Water breaks early before 37 weeks of pregnancy

explanation: PROM describes when the amniotic sac breaks open before any labor contractions begin in a full-term pregnancy. [learn more](BMP311_U2_T1#BMP311_U2_T1_h2)

question: What change in monthly periods do many clients using a levonorgestrel IUCD notice after a few months?

options.A: A significant reduction in bleeding or complete stoppage
options.B: Unpredictable flooding that requires surgical repair
options.C: Extremely heavy and painful monthly periods
options.D: Permanent cessation of all ovarian function

explanation: Because the hormone thins the uterine lining, many users experience much lighter periods or even amenorrhea over time. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T9#BMP224_U3_T9_h2)

question: What physical change happens inside the chest cavity when the diaphragm contracts?

options.A: It stays the exact same size while ribs move.
options.B: It enlarges, causing air to rush into the lungs.
options.C: It shrinks completely, forcing all air outward.
options.D: It turns into solid bone to protect the heart.

explanation: Flattening the diaphragm increases thoracic volume, lowering pressure and drawing air inward. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T9#BMP111_U3_T9_h4)

question: How does fair duty rostering relate directly to the staffing management function?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any further staff training
options.B: It forces doctors to take over all midwifery duties
options.C: It balances workloads and helps prevent staff burnout
options.D: It increases the financial revenue of the clinic

explanation: Managing human resources involves protecting worker well-being through equitable schedules that prevent extreme exhaustion. [learn more](BMP312_U1_T5#BMP312_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why might a normal non-pregnant serum creatinine level be a warning sign during pregnancy?

options.A: Normal pregnancy lowers creatinine levels, so a standard value actually reflects reduced kidney function
options.B: Pregnancy causes the liver to produce excess creatinine which masks kidney disease
options.C: Creatinine is never measured in pregnant women because it is completely unreliable
options.D: Standard values are too low to detect normal fetal kidney waste elimination

explanation: Because healthy pregnant kidneys filter blood much faster, normal serum creatinine drops. A value in the upper normal non-pregnant range actually points to sluggish kidney function. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T10#BMP221_U4_T10_h1)

question: Which major protective agent is abundant in breast milk to line the baby's gut against infections?

options.A: Hemoglobin
options.B: Secretory IgA
options.C: Fibrinogen
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Secretory IgA is an antibody that survives the baby's digestive tract to line the mucous membranes, blocking bacteria and viruses from entering the body. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T3#BMP214_U3_T3_h2)

question: What is the main difference that separates protozoa from bacteria?

options.A: The total absence of any genetic material
options.B: A defined nucleus and organelles
options.C: A rigid outer peptidoglycan wall
options.D: A capsule made of thick polysaccharide

explanation: Protozoa are eukaryotic cells, meaning they have a true membrane-bound nucleus and internal parts, unlike bacteria which are prokaryotic. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T4#BMP116_U3_T4_h1)

question: A community midwife finishes assisting a difficult breech delivery at midnight. When should she document the details of the birth?

options.A: Only if the baby develops complications later in the first week
options.B: At the end of the week when she prepares the monthly summary
options.C: As soon as possible while the details are still fresh in her mind
options.D: Next morning during the official change of shift handover meeting

explanation: Contemporaneous documentation ensures vital clinical details are captured accurately before memory fades. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T4#BMP227_U2_T4_h2)

question: A 38-year-old woman who smokes heavily and has frequent migraines wants family planning. Which method is most appropriate?

options.A: High-dose estrogen patches
options.B: Combined oral contraceptive pills
options.C: Progestin-only pills
options.D: Any standard combined hormonal method

explanation: Smoking combined with age over 35 and migraines makes estrogen-containing contraceptives unsafe due to stroke risk, making POPs the ideal choice. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T5#BMP224_U3_T5_h3)

question: At what level of an organization does administration mainly operate?

options.A: Mid-level
options.B: Floor-level
options.C: Top-level
options.D: Student-level

explanation: Administration is a top-level function involving boards and directors who set overarching policies and secure resources. [learn more](BMP312_U1_T1#BMP312_U1_T1_h4)

question: What physical assessment checks the function of cranial nerve V in a patient?

options.A: Listening to lung sounds with a stethoscope placed over the neck
options.B: Asking the patient to raise their eyebrows as high as possible
options.C: Shining a bright light into each pupil to check light reflex
options.D: Palpating the masseter muscles while the patient clenches their jaw

explanation: The trigeminal nerve controls the muscles of mastication, which are tested by feeling jaw-clenching strength. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T7#BMP111_U3_T7_h5)

question: Why must a midwife avoid warming a hypothermic baby too quickly?

options.A: Rapid warming can cause sudden low blood pressure and breathing pauses
options.B: Quick heating stops breast milk production in mothers
options.C: Sudden warmth causes the baby's skin to peel off
options.D: Fast heat changes always trigger immediate jaundice

explanation: Warming too fast dilates blood vessels rapidly, dropping blood pressure and risking apnea in fragile newborns. [learn more](BMP220_U3_T3#BMP220_U3_T3_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended strategy for overcoming security or access barriers in community midwifery?

options.A: Partnering with local community leaders for safe transit
options.B: Planning visits during daylight hours with local guides
options.C: Mapping out reliable routes before leaving the health facility
options.D: Ignoring local security warnings to prove professional bravery

explanation: Midwives must prioritize personal safety and should never ignore security warnings or travel into volatile areas unprepared. [learn more](BMP227_U1_T2#BMP227_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is it unhelpful to force a survivor into taking immediate legal action against their abuser?

options.A: It prevents the midwife from documenting physical injuries properly
options.B: It violates international nursing licensing regulations and bylaws
options.C: It guarantees that the abuser will apologize and change their behavior
options.D: It can strip away their sense of control and cause further psychological trauma

explanation: Survivors need autonomy and control over their choices; pressuring them mimics the powerlessness of the abuse itself. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T4#BMP310_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why are synthetic prostaglandins usually placed directly into the vagina or cervix instead of being swallowed as regular pills?

options.A: Pills take too long to dissolve in the stomach fluids of pregnant women
options.B: Oral tablets cause severe damage to the lining of the human stomach
options.C: They break down very quickly near where they are made in local tissues
options.D: Direct application prevents the liver from filtering out the active drug

explanation: Prostaglandins have a very short lifespan in the body, so placing them right at the target organ ensures they work effectively before they degrade. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which right is specifically restricted for a patient admitted on an involuntary basis?

options.A: Freedom of movement and personal liberty
options.B: The right to be free from physical abuse
options.C: Protection of personal privacy and dignity
options.D: The right to receive humane medical treatment

explanation: Involuntary admission legally restricts a person's freedom of movement and liberty to ensure safety during a mental health crisis. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T4#BMP223_U1_T4_h4)

question: A woman in her third trimester has mild ankle swelling after standing for a long time. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Complete absence of antidiuretic hormone secretion
options.B: Total renal failure caused by high dietary salt intake
options.C: Compression of pelvic veins by the enlarging uterus
options.D: Severe intracellular dehydration of all lower limb tissues

explanation: The heavy uterus presses on pelvic blood vessels, slowing blood return from the legs and causing normal ankle swelling. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T4#BMP121_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is the immediate response of a blood vessel right after it is cut or injured?

options.A: Vasoconstriction
options.B: Capillary proliferation
options.C: Vasodilation
options.D: Endothelial swelling

explanation: Blood vessels immediately narrow by contracting their muscles to slow down blood loss before a clot can form. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T4#BMP111_U5_T4_h4)

question: Why is worker rehabilitation a core goal of occupational health?

options.A: To lower the cost of manufacturing goods in local factories
options.B: To replace older workers with younger members of the labor force
options.C: To support injured or ill workers in returning to productive employment safely
options.D: To penalize employers who fail to provide safety gear on site

explanation: Rehabilitation helps employees recover fully and transition back to their jobs without re-injury. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T1#BMP126_U4_T1_h4)

question: A mother brings in a toddler who is irritable, has sunken eyes, and drinks eagerly from a cup. Which clinical classification fits these findings?

options.A: Severe dehydration
options.B: Some dehydration
options.C: Hypervolemic overload
options.D: No active dehydration

explanation: Irritability, sunken eyes, and eager drinking are classic signs of moderate fluid deficits, matching the classification for some dehydration. [learn more](BMP222_U3_T2#BMP222_U3_T2_h4)

question: What does 'validity' mean when discussing written exams?

options.A: The students finish answering all questions within the time limit
options.B: The final scores are posted on the notice board on time
options.C: The test accurately measures what it is supposed to measure
options.D: The exam papers are printed clearly without spelling errors

explanation: Validity ensures that a clinical test assesses real midwifery capability rather than unrelated traits like writing speed. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T9#BMP312_U3_T9_h6)

question: What is the traditional shape and design of an air-ring cushion?

options.A: A long rectangular wedge made of dense memory foam
options.B: A small square pad filled with cooling gel beads
